### Problem 1

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
library(patchwork)
library(ggridges)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.width = 6,
  fig.asp = .6,
  out.width = "90%"
)

theme_set(theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom"))

options(
  ggplot2.continuous.colour = "viridis",
  ggplot2.continuous.fill = "viridis"
)
```

```{r load_noaa}
data("ny_noaa")
```

```{r }
## A noaa sumnary
n_rows = nrow(ny_noaa)
n_cols = ncol(ny_noaa)
n_stations = n_distinct(pull(ny_noaa, id))
first_date = min(pull(ny_noaa, date))
last_date = max(pull(ny_noaa, date))
pct_missing_prcp = round(mean(is.na(pull(ny_noaa, prcp))) * 100, 1)
pct_missing_snow = round(mean(is.na(pull(ny_noaa, snow))) * 100, 1)
pct_missing_tmax = round(mean(is.na(pull(ny_noaa, tmax))) * 100, 1)
```

The dataset contains daily weather records from 747 weather stations in New York, from 1981-01-01 to 2010-12-31. It has 2595176 rows and 7 columns. Missing data is a major issue, especially for maximum temperature, 43.7% of values are missing, compared with 14.7% of snowfall and 5.6% of precipitation values.

```{r}
## Data cleaning
ny_noaa |> drop_na(tmax) |> pull(tmax) |> head()

noaa_df =
  ny_noaa |> separate(date, into = c("year", "month", "day"), sep = "-") |>
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),
    month = as.numeric(month),
    day = as.numeric(day),
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = prcp / 10)
```

### For snowfall, what are the most commonly observed values? Why?

```{r snow_common}
noaa_df |>
  count(snow) |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```

The most common snowfall value is 0, because it does not snow on most days 
of the year. 


### Make a two-panel plot showing the average max temperature in January and in July in each station across years. Is there any observable / interpretable structure? Any outliers?

```{r warning = FALSE}
noaa_df |>
  filter(month == 1 | month == 7) |>
  mutate(month = case_match(month, 1 ~ "January", 7 ~ "July")) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  drop_na(mean_tmax) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .3, size = .5) +
  geom_line(alpha = .3) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Average max temperature by station",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average max temperature in °C"
  )
```

Average max temperatures in July is around 25–30°C and are much higher than in 
January (-5 to 5°C), and January varies more from year to year. 
There are a few outliers, such as individual stations with a super
cold July or January compared with others in the same year.


### Make a two-panel plot showing (i) tmax vs tmin for the full dataset (note that a scatterplot may not be the best option); and (ii) make a plot showing the distribution of snowfall values greater than 0 and less than 100 separately by year.

```{r warning = FALSE, fig.asp = 1}
tmax_tmin_plot =
  noaa_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_hex() +
  labs(
    title = "Max vs. min temperature",
    x = "Min temp (°C)",
    y = "Max temp (°C)"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

snow_plot =
  noaa_df |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  mutate(year = factor(year)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = snow, y = year)) +
  geom_density_ridges(scale = .85) +
  labs(
    title = "Snowfall by year",
    x = "Snowfall (mm)",
    y = "Year"
  )

tmax_tmin_plot + snow_plot
```
